gradeScale.RECOMMENDED: passes all hard gates and the quality bar with the best available evidence for Forge's job
gradeScale.GOOD ENOUGH: passes all hard gates; quality bar met only by extrapolation/judgement, or dominated on price by an equivalent
gradeScale.NOT SUITABLE: fails a hard gate, or evidence says it misses the quality bar

meta.important: No model was tested by Forge or by any study on Indian home food, Indian labels or Forge's own safety prompts. Every grade marked judgement=true is an inference from the cited evidence about related versions, not a measurement.

FOOD_PHOTO.basis: 4 photos/day x 30; 1 image (~1,500 tok) + ~800 tok prompt/schema; ~400 tok JSON

LABEL.basis: 1/day x 30; 1 image + prompt; ~500 tok per-field JSON

COACH.basis: 3/day x 30; ~10k tok context (upper end of 6-10k), no prompt caching assumed; ~500 tok reply

PROGRAM.basis: one ~30-page PDF as text (~40k tok) -> ~8k tok program JSON

meta.costMethod: USD/month = sum(calls x (inTok x inPerM + outTok x outPerM) / 1e6) at the verified list price in closed.json/open.json. Image tokens are assumed ~1,500 per photo for all providers and billed as input (real counts vary by provider). No prompt caching assumed. reasoningHeavyAllJobs triples output tokens to bound hidden reasoning tokens. OpenRouter platform fees are not included (not verified).

evidenceKeys.V26: Vedovelli et al., Sci Rep 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41598-026-58755-w) - 30+ VLMs on Nutrition5k; model choice explains 99.6% of variance
evidenceKeys.C25: Coburn et al., arXiv 2507.07048 v2 - ACETADA calorie MAPE: GPT-4.1 23.3%, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 23.9%, Gemma-3 27B 27.7%, Qwen2.5-VL 72B 33.9%, LLaMA-3.2-V 66%
evidenceKeys.RJ25: Rodriguez-Jimenez et al., Nutrients 2025 - ChatGPT-5 image-only energy MAPE 30.5%, 13.9% with ingredient list
evidenceKeys.F25: Fridolfsson et al., Curr Dev Nutr 2025 - systematic underestimation growing with portion size
evidenceKeys.SF26: Gravellier et al. (SeeFood), medRxiv 2026 preprint - real-world photos 52-90%+ MAPE for all models; GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, Llama-4-Maverick finalists
evidenceKeys.S26: Sterling et al., bioRxiv 2026 preprint (abstract only) - Gemini 3.0 Flash CCC 0.767; Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite CCC 0.754
evidenceKeys.N26: Nakagawa & Yamamoto, Nutrients 2026 - Claude Haiku 4.5 energy R2 0.23 vs Sonnet 4.6 0.60; Sonnet within 1-3 MedAPE points of Opus
evidenceKeys.M26: Marchetti et al., Nutrients 2026 - open 4-9B VLMs within ~20-35% of frontier portion error; sub-2B/LLaVA-era unusable
evidenceKeys.OF26: OmniFood-Bench, arXiv 2607.08423 - catastrophic mass-estimation failure across 6 VLMs incl. qwen3-vl-8B, gpt-5.1
evidenceKeys.JMIR26: Nakagawa & Yamamoto, JMIR preprint 116178 - 4-bit 4B on-device VLM ~36-44% energy MedAPE (UNVERIFIED)
evidenceKeys.A25: Assiri et al., J Imaging 2025 - 2024-era models 83-90% of English label element-value pairs correct after post-processing
evidenceKeys.MJ22: Majmudar et al., NPJ Digit Med 2022 - purpose-built CNN 2.16 %BF MAE vs DXA; no general VLM validated (evidence gap)
evidenceKeys.RAND25: McBain et al., Psychiatric Services 2025 (RAND) - suicide-question alignment; Claude fewer high-risk direct answers than ChatGPT; Gemini most restrictive
evidenceKeys.OAI25: OpenAI 2025 (vendor self-report) - GPT-5 self-harm compliance 91% vs 77%
evidenceKeys.MPACT26: mPACT 2026 (UNVERIFIED, press only) - Claude Sonnet 4.5 best, GPT-5.2 most consistent; Grok 4.1 and Mistral Medium 3 weakest; ED weakest area for all
evidenceKeys.W26: Wang et al., arXiv 2611.10488 preprint - ED safety: GLM-5.2 82.8%, Gemma-4-31B 79.5%, Qwen3.6-27B 67.7%
evidenceKeys.P26: Pucci et al., arXiv 2606.02444 - 7-9B open models (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B) unsafe in 30-90% of risky-cell advice
evidenceKeys.Y25: Yim et al., Int J Eat Disord 2025 - all chatbots (GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral) produced some harmful ED content
evidenceKeys.JSB25: JSONSchemaBench arXiv 2501.10868 - only provider-side constrained decoding gives ~100% schema compliance; prompt-only 13-21% on hard schemas
evidenceKeys.IFS25: IFScale arXiv 2507.11538 - instruction-following decays with rule density; small models worst
evidenceKeys.ORSO: OpenRouter structured-outputs doc - strict enforced only where upstream supports it; needs require_parameters
evidenceKeys.GROQSO: Groq structured-outputs doc - strict constrained decoding on gpt-oss-20b/120b, qwen3.8-27b

allJobs_hardGates: G1 Reachable today by Forge: Anthropic native, or an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions base URL + key (on-device runtimes fail this until LiteRT-LM/llama.cpp is integrated).
G2 Lifecycle: not a preview, not closed to new users, not shutting down within ~6 months, and has a verified price.

G3 No training on user data on the tier used: dataPolicy 'no-train' (Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Alibaba Model Studio, OpenRouter with ZDR enforced, DeepInfra non-Google, Groq) or Gemini with a billing-enabled key. 'unclear' fails (Mistral direct, Cerebras, qwen3.8-flash, glm-4.6v). Applies to text jobs too because COACH/PLAN carry health data.

G4 Output contract: Forge expects JSON; FOOD_PHOTO/LABEL/BODY/PLAN/PROGRAM need provider-side constrained json_schema or reliable JSON mode (prompt-only JSON fails: JSONSchemaBench 13-21% compliance on hard schemas). Forge keeps tolerant extraction + Kotlin validation + one retry for every model.

hardGates: photos not trained on (photo rules + task brief)
FOOD_PHOTO.qualityBar: Good enough = a model whose own family/tier has published single-photo energy error in the frontier band (~23-36% MAPE on curated mixed meals, or CCC >= ~0.75 on Nutrition5k). Rationale: Forge biases high, clamps every number, and the user edits before saving, so the model only needs to identify foods and give a portion-sane first guess; but model choice explains 99.6% of accuracy variance (V26) and cheap/small tiers can collapse (Haiku 4.5 R2 0.23; sub-2B unusable), so a vision model from a family with no food evidence is NOT SUITABLE until it passes Forge's own 20-meal Indian test (target: median abs error <= 35% vs weighed/label values, no systematic under-call > 15% after Forge's margin).

hardGates: G1-G4 with constrained per-field schema (units separate)
LABEL.qualityBar: Near-exact transcription: target >= 95% of element-value pairs exact on a 20-label test; Forge must Atwater-check (4/4/9 vs stated kcal, flag > 15% mismatch) and always show a confirm screen. Only 2024-era evidence exists (83-90% pairs correct), so every grade is a judgement; RECOMMENDED reserved for mid/frontier closed models with strict schema.

hardGates: strongest privacy available (guardrail photo_feature_blocked_groups says photos stay on the device unless exported: treat a cloud call as an explicit, consented export, ZDR/no-train only; on-device preferred)
never attractiveness/appearance commentary (photo_no_attractiveness_commentary) - enforced by schema with no free-text appearance field + post-filter
BODY.qualityBar: Honest range only: the model returns a point estimate or range in a strict schema; Forge widens to +/-6 points (photo_bf_accuracy_limits), labels it rough/unvalidated, uses the LOWER bound for safety. No general VLM is validated vs DXA, so no model is RECOMMENDED; GOOD ENOUGH = passes gates and does not refuse/comment.

hardGates: G1-G4 with the phase field as a string enum enforced by constrained decoding where possible
PLAN.qualityBar: Strict enum adherence (100% after code validation, retry once, else rule-based fallback); rationale text passes safety_messaging_no_praise_for_restriction / no_body_shaming filter. RECOMMENDED where the provider guarantees the enum (Anthropic, OpenAI strict, Groq strict).

hardGates: acceptable ED/crisis behaviour: positive published evidence for the exact model, its direct predecessor or its vendor family at frontier tier; families with negative evidence (Grok, Mistral, Qwen, Llama, sub-10B open) or no evidence at all (DeepSeek, Kimi, MiMo, gpt-oss) fail until they pass Forge's own red-team set (Winecoff & Klyman 7-category taxonomy, incl. 'for a friend' framing)
COACH.qualityBar: Code always pre-empts: safety_crisis_disclosure cue detection stops coaching and shows Tele MANAS 14416 / 1800-89-14416 and 112; every reply passes the no-praise-for-restriction and no-body-shaming blocklist + classifier and regenerates on hit. Put safety rules first in the prompt (IFScale primacy), pass SCOFF status/BMI band (W26: +10-14 points). RECOMMENDED = family with the best crisis evidence at mid/frontier tier.

hardGates: enough max output for the program JSON (>= 16K)
PROGRAM.qualityBar: Complete extraction of every day/exercise/sets/reps from a long PDF into schema; Forge validates counts and training_* rules. No direct benchmark; graded on context, schema support and tier (judgement).

recommendedDefault.why: One first-party no-train provider Forge already calls natively, constrained JSON, best crisis evidence for COACH, Sonnet-tier food evidence. Cost is ~$3-4/month, so quality not price should decide.

cheapestPassingEveryJob.note: Literal minimum by computed cost among GOOD ENOUGH+ grades; uses several OpenRouter ZDR endpoints.

cheapestSensible.why: One open model, one key (OpenRouter with ZDR + require_parameters), passes every job: best-evidenced open food family, 79.5% ED-safety score for COACH.

cheapestFirstParty.why: No OpenRouter dependency: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite (paid key) has the best direct food evidence at its price; GPT-6 Luna for the rest.

freeNearFree.free: Truly free = on-device Gemma 4 E4B for FOOD_PHOTO/LABEL/BODY after LiteRT-LM integration ($0, private), but COACH/PROGRAM still need a cloud model (~$0.10/month on gemma-4-31b ZDR). Gemini free tier and OpenRouter ':free' variants are excluded because they train on or do not protect data.

fullyPrivate.target: BODY (and optionally FOOD_PHOTO/LABEL) on-device Gemma 4 E4B via LiteRT-LM; COACH/PLAN/PROGRAM on Anthropic (no-train by default).
